public_rationale: He said OpenAI 'cannot afford to pay for the compute' in Oracle's data centers. A September 2025 report said the roughly $300B, five-year Oracle contract begins in 2027 (e1). So most payments were not yet due at the 17 March 2026 post. In February 2026, OpenAI announced $110B in committed funding (e2). That weighs against an inability to pay in the near term. On 31 March 2026, after the post, OpenAI said the round had closed at $122B. The same report said OpenAI was still burning cash (e2). A September 2026 report citing the FT said OpenAI was on track to use up that funding by 2028 (e3). That is a projection about later years, not a missed payment. The packet has no Oracle payment schedule. It has no report of a missed, deferred or renegotiated payment. It does not show what OpenAI owed Oracle in early 2026 or whether OpenAI paid it. The evidence does not settle the claim either way.
limitations: Oracle's payment schedule for OpenAI is not public. The packet does not show any amounts due between 1 January and 17 March 2026.
Committed funding is not the same as cash on hand. The packet does not show how much of the round had been paid in by the post date.
The figures come from news reports about a private company. They are not audited.
The FT-reported runway is a projection from a deal presentation. It is not a record of payments.

statement.document_title: Why Are We Still Doing This?

The Oracle contract (about $300B over five years) mostly begins in 2027. So affordability is largely about future payments, which an observation as of March 2026 cannot settle.
Period: the state at the post date. I use early 2026 up to 2026-03-17, the latest financial picture before the post. This choice is flagged.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that OpenAI missed, deferred or renegotiated payments due to Oracle for lack of funds, or could not raise the money needed for payments then due.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that OpenAI was paying what was due to Oracle and had cash and committed funding enough to cover the payments falling due.

evidence.explanation: The same article says the contract begins in 2027, so most payments fall due after the post. Whether OpenAI can afford them is largely a future question.

evidence.explanation: Around the post date OpenAI had about $110B (later $122B) in committed funding. That counts against near-term inability to pay, though the same article says it was still burning cash and unprofitable.
